race.name: The Gravel of Marathon
race.tagline: Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier: two laps of a 31 km loop around Lake Marathon, three-quarters of it on dirt.

vitals.start_format: UCI Gravel World Series age-category competition; exact wave schedule not published
vitals.registration: Registration is open through the organizer-linked ENDU platform for both official distances.
vitals.entry_fee: Not stated on the cited public organizer page
route_options: Long: 95.9 km / 59.6 mi with 1,520 m / 4,987 ft, about 75% off-road, two laps of the 31 km loop — qualifier for elites, men 19-59, and women 19-49
Short: 65.6 km / 40.8 mi with 1,130 m / 3,707 ft, about 75% off-road, one lap of the 31 km loop — qualifier for men 60+ and women 50+

climate.description: Mid-November in Attica is generally cooler than summer, but rain can turn the soft lake-edge dirt and farm roads into a different course. The race-specific forecast remains the authority close to the event.
challenges: Limited daylight late in the season

terrain.primary: Lake dirt, farm roads, and a rocky opening climb
terrain.surface: About 75% of the course is dirt: rocky ground on the opening climb, farm roads that switch between dirt and asphalt, two shallow streams, and 4 km of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon. [5]
features: A 2 km rocky climb averaging 6%, with a 9% maximum
A shallow stream and a hard 500 m climb before the loop
4 km of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon
Two laps of the 31 km loop on the long course

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The inaugural Greek UCI qualifier publishes a detailed course, three-quarters dirt with real climbing for its length. The unproven first-edition field and operations record hold it in Tier 3.

logistics.explanation: Marathon is roughly 40 km from Athens with broad local lodging choices, which is much easier than most destination gravel races. Airport transfer, city traffic, and bike transport still require planning, but the event is not remote.

length.explanation: The long course is 95.9 km, or 59.6 miles, just inside the published 40-60 mile score-two band [5]. Two laps and a retraced approach make it a short race with a long-race pacing problem.

technicality.explanation: About 75% of the course is dirt: rocky ground on the opening climb, farm roads that switch between dirt and asphalt, two shallow streams, soft lakeside dirt, and a 12% soft-dirt ramp [5]. It asks for mixed-surface control without singletrack.

elevation.explanation: The long course climbs 1,520 metres, about 4,987 feet, inside the 4,000-6,000-foot score-three band [5]. It comes as a rocky climb out of Marathon, short ramps on each lap, and the climb back over Grammatiko [5][6].

climate.explanation: November reduces the heat risk around Attica, while rain could materially change the 90-percent off-road surface. Conditions deserve equipment flexibility but are not inherently an extreme-climate challenge.

altitude.explanation: The course tops out below 400 metres. The 12% ramp hurts because it comes back on lap two, not because oxygen is scarce.

adventure.explanation: The race joins Lake Marathon, farm tracks, two stream crossings, Grammatiko and the town of the Battle of Marathon. A repeated loop usually costs adventure, but this one has strong place identity.

prestige.explanation: This is Greece's first UCI Gravel World Series race and a qualifier for the 2027 Worlds. That matters immediately, but an inaugural event has no race history or established status of its own.

race_quality.explanation: Bicycle Friendly Greece and the MBike team bring cycling-media and Athens Bike Festival experience, while the official course package is unusually specific. Actual race-day execution remains unproven until November.

experience.explanation: Starting at Marathon Stadium, riding beside the lake, fording streams and finishing in central Marathon gives each 31 km lap a real narrative without relying on invented crowd claims.

community.explanation: The organizer has supported Greek cycling media since 1999 and the Athens Bike Festival since 2010. The specific gravel race is brand new, so established-organizer reach should not be confused with a mature race community.

field_depth.explanation: UCI qualification should draw strong Greek and regional age-group racers, but no start list or field size is published. The series status supports a competitive score, not a claim of elite international depth.

value.explanation: A 95.9 km UCI qualifier on three-quarters dirt, with a detailed official course and downloadable GPX files, is a substantial product. With no public entry price in the cited pages, the honest score is neutral.

expenses.explanation: Athens is internationally accessible and Marathon has varied lodging, but flights, bike transport, and multiple nights make this a high-cost trip for non-European athletes. Regional riders will spend much less.

course_description.character: The course leaves Marathon Stadium, crosses town and climbs 2 km on rocky ground at 6% (9% at the steepest) [5]. It passes Grammatiko, runs 5 km of asphalt, fords a shallow stream and climbs a hard 500 m to the start of a 31 km loop [5]. Each lap is 16 km of farm road alternating dirt and asphalt, 4 km of soft dirt beside Lake Marathon, a second stream, a 200 m climb on soft dirt at up to 12%, and 6 km of dirt back to the loop start [5]. The long course rides the loop twice, the short course once, and both retrace the approach through Grammatiko and Ano Souli to finish in central Marathon [5][6].
course_description.signature_challenge: Keeping enough for the second lap: the 12% soft-dirt climb comes back near mile 45, and the climb out of the loop toward Grammatiko still stands between you and the descent home [5][6].

suffering_zones.label: Rocky opening climb
suffering_zones.desc: Two kilometres on rocky ground at 6%, touching 9%, right after the start [5].

suffering_zones.label: Lake Marathon
suffering_zones.desc: Four kilometres of soft dirt beside the lake after 16 km of mixed farm road [5].

suffering_zones.label: 12% surprise
suffering_zones.desc: Past the greenhouses and a second shallow stream, 200 metres of soft dirt climbing at up to 12% [5].

suffering_zones.label: Second-lap climb
suffering_zones.desc: The same 12% soft-dirt ramp on lap two, with the return over Grammatiko still to come [5][6].

official_route.name: The Gravel of Marathon 95 km route

biased_opinion.summary: Two laps sound less adventurous until you look at the lap: farm roads, soft lake dirt, a stream and a 12% ramp, all after a rocky climb out of Marathon. The repeat format makes pacing legible. Spend lap one carelessly and lap two, plus the ride home over Grammatiko, collects the debt.
strengths: Detailed official course and GPX files
Easy access from Athens relative to most gravel destinations
weaknesses: Current public page omits aid and cutoff details
biased_opinion.bottom_line: One of the strongest new-race intakes in the catalog because the organizer published the actual demands. Tier 3 today; the first edition will decide whether it deserves more.

logistics.airport: Athens International Airport (ATH), with Marathon approximately 40 km northeast of central Athens
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Marathon, Nea Makri, or the Schinias area for a short race-morning transfer; Athens works only if you plan traffic and parking carefully.
logistics.transport: A rental car or confirmed event transfer is the practical option with a bike.
logistics.food: Marathon and the surrounding coast have restaurants and groceries. The loop has two feed stations; carry tested race nutrition for the approach and the ride home.

history.founder: Bicycle Friendly Greece and the MBike team
history.origin_story: Created as Greece's first UCI Gravel World Series event by a team with cycling-media and festival experience.
history.reputation: An inaugural event with an unusually transparent course package but no results history yet.

guide_variables.race_terrain: A rocky approach from Marathon, then two laps of a 31 km loop of farm roads, soft lake dirt, streams and a 12% ramp
guide_variables.race_weather: Mediterranean late autumn with meaningful rain risk

topics.lap_pacing: Splitting effort across two laps and the ride home
topics.climbing: A rocky 2 km opener and a repeated 12% soft-dirt ramp
topics.handling: Switching between rocky ground, soft dirt, streams, and asphalt
topics.weather: Adjusting tires and layers for November rain

marketplace_variables.race_hook: Train the second lap, not the first.
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: Seven race-specific plans for Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier: 95.9 km, 1,520 metres, and the same 12% ramp twice.

non_negotiables.why: The long course rides its 31 km loop twice, then retraces the approach home.
The 12% soft-dirt climb returns on lap two, after a rocky 2 km opener.
The course alternates rocky ground, soft lake dirt, farm roads, shallow streams, and asphalt.

final_verdict.one_liner: Greece's first UCI gravel qualifier has more verified course substance than many established races.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Race it if you want UCI stakes and can respect a repeat-lap pacing plan. Wait for first-edition results if operational certainty matters more than being early.
final_verdict.alternatives: Gravel of Loutraki for an established Greek gravel event; Alentejo Gravel for a later-season European UCI qualifier.
